answer: Every agent must lock a 500-POA stake bond in a slashing escrow before trading. First, it registers its public key and posts the bond. Second, peers audit its first 20 trades and may file a signed fraud claim. Third, a verified claim burns 250 POA and freezes it for 30 days. A farm spinning up 1,000 fakes risks 500,000 POA, roughly $12,500, just to enter, and one fraud costs each clone half its stake. The delta between honest profit and attack cost stays wide, and a cipher-signed trail traces every fake. Like a velvet rope at a club door, it looks soft, but only paying guests get in.
